# 1 Clement 61 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 1 Clement 61 (3 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Total disagreements logged:** 4

---

## V.1 — "excellent and unspeakable might" / "magnificent and indescribable dominion"
- **EMET:** "excellent and unspeakable might" / **LOGOS:** "magnificent and indescribable dominion" / **PNEUMA:** "magnificent and inexpressible might"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Magnificent and indescribable dominion" (LOGOS) — the Greek *megaloprepous kai anexichniastou dynasteias* uses *dynasteia* (power, dominion). "Dominion" is more precise than "might." "Magnificent" for *megaloprepēs* is correct. "Indescribable" for *anexichniastos* (untraceable/unsearchable/beyond description) is appropriate.

---

## V.1 — "harmony" / "concord" / "harmony"
- **EMET/PNEUMA:** "harmony" / **LOGOS:** "concord"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Harmony" (EMET/PNEUMA) — the Greek *homonoian* means "same-mindedness/concord/harmony." "Harmony" is slightly more natural in English; "concord" (LOGOS) is an exact Latin equivalent but less immediate.

---

## V.3 — "Guardian" / "Advocate" / "Protector"
- **EMET:** "Guardian of our souls" / **LOGOS:** "Advocate of our souls" / **PNEUMA:** "Protector of our souls"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Advocate of our souls" (LOGOS) — the Greek *prostasias* in the genitive means "advocacy/patronage." In the context of Christ standing before the Father for human souls, "Advocate" is the most theologically precise rendering, paralleling 1 John 2:1 (*paraklētos*).

---

## V.3 — Doxological formula length
- **EMET:** "now and unto all generations and for ever and ever" / **LOGOS:** "both now and unto all generations and for ever and ever" / **PNEUMA:** "now and through all generations, forever and ever"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Now and unto all generations and for ever and ever" (EMET without "both") — the expanded formula should be rendered precisely. "Unto" preserves the archaic liturgical register appropriate for a doxological close. "Both now" (LOGOS) adds an unnecessary conjunction; PNEUMA's "through all generations" changes the Greek *eis pasas tas geneas*.

---

*— SOPHIA*
